gap: No result ChatGPT got states which of these 11-inch tablets can send video out of the USB-C port to a monitor. Samsung's own DeX FAQ says the Tab S11 series and Tab A11+ work with a 'DeX cable or HDMI cable', while the Tab S10 FE/FE+ and Tab S10 Lite 'are not compatible with HDMI output' or with Wireless DeX. Lenovo's spec sheet lists the Yoga Tab's port as 'USB 3.2 Gen 1, with charging, DP-Out'. Samsung gives the A11+'s port as USB 2.0, and owners on Samsung's own forum report it has no wired video out.
standout_why: I read three pages. Tech Advisor (cited, updated 2026-11-10) gives update years, the S Pen and charging for the Tab S11, but nothing on USB-C version, video out or DeX on a monitor, and it doesn't cover the Yoga Tab. iTechGuides (cited, 2026-08-18) says DeX Extended Mode works with a monitor on the Tab S11 Ultra only. It gives no port or video-out details for the 11-inch Tab S11, A11+ or S10 FE, and doesn't mention the S10 FE's missing HDMI output. ChatGPT's own answer recommends the A11+ for 'everyday apps' and the Yoga Tab 'for productivity' without saying whether either can drive a monitor. I could not read the text of Android Central, Tom's Guide (both pages), TechRadar's Tab S11 review or Wired (Wired blocked fetching), so I can't rule out that one of them mentions it.
decides: This only matters for a shopper who wants to plug the tablet into a monitor or TV, as a laptop stand-in with DeX or a desktop setup. For that shopper, the Tab S11 ($899.99 in ChatGPT's card, not re-checked) and the Lenovo Yoga Tab ($599.99 at Best Buy in ChatGPT's card, not re-checked) both have a USB 3.2 Gen 1 port and the maker lists wired video out or HDMI DeX. That makes the Yoga Tab the cheapest confirmed way to do it. The Galaxy Tab S10 FE, which Dealectric already lists, is ruled out by Samsung's own words: no HDMI output and no Wireless DeX. The A11+ is uncertain. Samsung's FAQ lists it for HDMI DeX, but its spec page says USB 2.0, Samsung's US business page calls its DeX the 'Standalone Edition', and several owners on Samsung's forum say a wired monitor doesn't work. The page should not promise wired monitor use on the A11+. For a shopper who only watches video and browses, none of this changes the pick.

findings.label: Wired HDMI output and Wireless DeX
findings.value: Not supported: 'The Galaxy Tab S9 FE, Tab S9 FE+, Tab S10 FE, Tab S10 FE+, and Tab S10 Lite are not compatible with HDMI output.' The Wireless DeX section repeats the same exclusion.
findings.source_title: Frequently asked questions about Samsung DeX (Samsung US)
findings.note: Samsung's wording, quoted. The page shows no last-updated date. A 'Recommended Articles' blurb on the same page says the S10 FE has DeX built in. That means DeX on the tablet's own screen, which doesn't contradict the exclusion from HDMI output.

findings.label: Wired DeX to a TV or monitor (DeX cable or HDMI cable)
findings.value: Supported. The Tab S11 series is in Samsung's list of tablets that work over a DeX cable or HDMI cable, and in its Wireless DeX list.
findings.source_title: Frequently asked questions about Samsung DeX (Samsung US)
findings.note: The same FAQ says 'DeX Pad and DeX Station is not supported on Android 16 and One UI 8'. That covers Samsung's DeX accessories, not a plain HDMI cable.

findings.label: DeX Extended Mode (dual screen with a monitor)
findings.value: Samsung UK credits it to the Ultra only: 'the Tab S11 Ultra can now be paired with an external monitor to create a true dual-screen setup.'
findings.source_title: What are the features of the Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra and Tab S11? (Samsung UK)
findings.note: A search snippet from Samsung's launch release says Extended Mode is a 'Galaxy Tab S11 series' feature. I couldn't open the release (timeout), so I'm going by the support page I did read.

findings.label: Core specs
findings.value: 11-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2X, up to 120 Hz; MediaTek Dimensity 9400+; 8,400 mAh, 45 W; 12 GB RAM with 128/256/512 GB; microSD up to 2 TB; 'S Pen (BLE not supported) in-box'
findings.source_title: What are the features of the Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra and Tab S11? (Samsung UK)
findings.note: Values copied from the spec table. 'BLE not supported' means the included S Pen has no Bluetooth remote features.

findings.label: USB-C port and video out
findings.value: '1x USB-C (USB 5Gbps / USB 3.2 Gen 1), with charging, DP-Out and Audio'
findings.source_title: Lenovo PSREF: Yoga Tab spec (Last Modify Time 2025-08-12)
findings.note: Lenovo's spec sheet. The same page lists Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (QCM8650Q), an 11.1-inch 3200×2000 144 Hz LTPS display, 8 or 12 GB soldered RAM, an 8,860 mAh battery, the Lenovo Tab Pen Pro as a bundled accessory, and 'Android 15 or later'.

findings.label: USB version
findings.note: From the 'USB Version' spec field on the SM-X238U page. The same page lists 1920×1200, 7,040 mAh (typical) and microSD up to 2 TB. A USB 2.0-only port normally has no high-speed lanes to carry DisplayPort Alt Mode, so this agrees with the owner reports below. That explanation is my own reasoning, not Samsung's.

findings.label: Maker's DeX claims
findings.value: Samsung's US DeX FAQ lists the Tab A11+ under 'DeX cable or HDMI cable' and Wireless DeX. Samsung's US business product page says 'Samsung DeX Standalone Edition, a PC-like experience on your Tab' and says nothing about an external display. It lists '25W Super Fast Charging' with the charger sold separately.
findings.note: Samsung's own pages disagree with each other. The FAQ claim is at https://www.samsung.com/us/support/answer/ANS10001972/, also read 2026-11-11.

findings.label: Owner reports on wired monitor output (SM-X230)
findings.value: Owners report that a wired monitor doesn't work. jasonmiller11tt (2026-08-19): 'the SM-X230 does not have USB-C video output'. Chummy128 (2026-08-16): 'The USB don't support it.' No Samsung moderator has replied.
findings.source_title: A11 Dex with Monitor (Samsung US Community)
findings.note: These are user posts, not a reviewer's test. Use them only to qualify Samsung's FAQ claim, not as a measured result.
